Note::collapse_repeats¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::collapse_repeats() const

Reduce Every Run Of An Identical Character To One¶

collapse_repeats() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with every run of two or more of the same character in each cell reduced to a single copy. Use it to normalise “stretched” user text — "woooow", "!!!!", "----" — before matching, or as a rough de-duplication pass.

The operation is byte-level and unconditional: it does not know or care whether the repeated character is a letter, a digit, punctuation, a space, or part of a multi-byte character. So it also squashes real double letters — "book" becomes "bok", "hello" becomes "helo". Reach for it only when that trade-off is acceptable; use collapse_whitespace or collapse_punct when you want to collapse just one class.

collapse_repeats is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"woooow!!!", "aaabbbccc", "book"}).collapse_repeats())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["wow!", "abc", "bok"]

"book" → "bok" shows the trade-off: legitimate double letters collapse too.

See Also¶

  • Note::collapse_punct: collapse only runs of punctuation.

  • Note::collapse_whitespace / Note::collapse_spaces: collapse only whitespace.

  • Note::RegexAccessor::replace: regex().replace(R"((.)\1+)", "$1") for a Unicode-safe “collapse repeats” with more control.
